ev.q: Among 4,626 persons from participating outpatient clinics who received influenza testing during November 4–18, 2022, a total of 2,164 (47%) were children
Among household contacts exposed to someone with influenza, children were more than twice as likely to become ill
reaching 12.6 per 100,000 in children aged <5 years
who were more likely to receive a positive test result (33%; 714 of 2,164) than were adults (20%; 483 of 2,462)
Seasonal influenza vaccination coverage was low in both children (23%; 499 of 2,164) and adults
who were more likely to receive a positive test result (33%; 714 of 2,164) than were adults (20%; 483 of 2,462)
children were more likely to become ill than were adults (adjusted OR = 2.50; 95% CI = 1.55–4.03)
This report describes a field investigation conducted in Tennessee during November 2022
Persons who received a positive or negative influenza test result during November 4–18, 2022, were invited to complete a survey
Influenza activity increased earlier than usual among all age groups

methods_quotes.q: Factors associated with positive influenza test results in patients who received testing at participating clinics were identified using logistic regression.
Characteristics of household contacts were compared using logistic regression accounting for household clustering.
Secondary attack rates for symptomatic illness among household contacts with adjustment for age, vaccination status, and household size were assessed with a chain binomial model
For influenza-associated hospitalizations, a probability distribution constructed from the three highest weekly rates from each previous season
Hospitalization data from previous seasons were adjusted for underdetection using data on age group–specific testing practices
